decision.explanation: The claim posits that the combination of Omipalisib and Trametinib is predictive of sensitivity/response in NRAS-mutant melanoma. The available evidence (pmid-23431193) demonstrates that the combination of a MEK inhibitor (JTP-74057) and a PI3K/mTOR inhibitor (GSK2126458) produces synergistic anti-tumor effects in NRAS-mutant melanoma models. However, the specific agents Omipalisib and Trametinib are not tested in this source. While the drug classes match (Omipalisib is a PI3K/mTOR inhibitor and Trametinib is a MEK inhibitor), the specific drug identities differ. Therefore, the evidence supports the class-level combination but does not directly confirm the efficacy of the specific Omipalisib/Trametinib combination as written. This necessitates a revision of the claim to reflect that the evidence supports the class-level interaction rather than the specific named agents.

citations.quote: In six NRAS mutant melanoma cell lines, concomitant use of MEK inhibitor and PI3K/mTOR inhibitor resulted in greater decrease in cell viability than either alone, with the synergistic effect being marked in 4/6 cell lines. MEK inhibitor JTP-74057 and PI3K/mTOR inhibitor GSK2126458 together induced synergistic increase in apoptotic Annexin V+/PI+ cells in these cell lines. Tumor xenografts in nude mice were established with 5 of the 6 cell lines. Effects of single agent treatment with JTP-74057 or GSK2126458 ranged from minor inhibition to tumor stasis, while dual inhibitor treatment showed
synergistic effects in each case, with marked tumor reductions in 2/5 cases and the authors report one compete response in a MaMel301 cell line xenograft mouse.

The evidence supports the molecular context and class-level interaction but requires correction regarding the specific agents tested.

citations.quote: In six NRAS mutant melanoma cell lines, concomitant use of MEK inhibitor and PI3K/mTOR inhibitor resulted in greater decrease in cell viability than either alone, with the synergistic effect being marked in 4/6 cell lines. MEK inhibitor JTP-74057 and PI3K/mTOR inhibitor GSK2126458 together induced synergistic increase in apoptotic Annexin V+/PI+ cells in these cell lines. Tumor xenografts in nude mice were established with 5 of the 6 cell lines. Effects of single agent treatment with JTP-74057 or GSK2126458 ranged from minor inhibition to tumor stasis, while dual inhibitor treatment showed
synergistic effects in each case, with marked tumor reductions in 2/5 cases and the authors report one compete response in a MaMel301 cell line xenograft mouse.

This matches the claim's statement regarding the specific agents and outcomes found in the source.
